newsitem.title: NORWAY: Faeroe oil well more costly than forecast - Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Faeroe oil well more costly than forecast - Statoil.

text.p: Problems with drilling the Lopra-1 onshore well on the Faeroe Islands has raised the cost of the project by more than 40 percent, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the land well had come in at 12 million crowns over the original budget of 28 million crowns.
The well is operated by Dansk Olie og Naturgas (Dong), which is partnered by 18 other companies including Statoil.
According to Dong project manager Arne Rosenkrantz Larsen, technical problems with the well were encountered in the early phase of drilling, which began on July 13.

"The drill string got stuck at the bottom of the well in the final phase. We've been fishing for it over several weeks, but still haven't retrieved the last bit,' Larsen told Status Weekly. "To get on we've drilled a side-track around it."
The pilot well is expected to be completed by the end of October, he said.
The first section of Lopra-1 was drilled in the early 1980s to about 2,000 metres as part of a scientific project to characterise the geology of the Faeroese continental shelf.
Extending the well may yield useful geological data for oil companies participating in the first Faeroese offshore licensing round due in 1997, Statoil said.
